about: Sanity pairs for the content judge (docs/judge-calibration.md). Written and labelled by the Encore team (with Claude), not a rated dataset: each pair is one idea said two ways after the same earlier lines, 'strong' (a joke that turns its setup; a concrete image, sound or turn; a quotable point, a device or a call) and 'flat' (the same idea said plainly, of about the same length). The check is only whether a judge ranks strong above flat; ties count as half.

context: My landlord promised he'd fix the heating before winter.
pairs.strong: He didn't say which winter.
pairs.flat: It's still broken and it's cold.

context: I joined a gym in January.
The trainer asked me what my goals were.
pairs.strong: I said: to stop paying for this gym.
pairs.flat: I said: to get a bit fitter this year.

context: My dad has never once used a GPS.
pairs.strong: He says he doesn't need a woman's voice telling him where to go. He's got my mum for that.
pairs.flat: He says he prefers paper maps and his own memory of the roads, and he doesn't trust the phone.

context: I tried online dating for a month.
pairs.strong: Turns out my type is people who never reply.
pairs.flat: It didn't go well and I didn't meet anyone.

context: My phone says my screen time is up forty percent this week.
pairs.strong: It says it like a disappointed parent. Mate, you're the one I spent it with.
pairs.flat: I should probably try to use my phone a bit less in the evenings.

context: I bought a self-help book called How to Finish What You Start.
pairs.strong: I'm on chapter one. I've been on chapter one for two years.
pairs.flat: I've only read a little of it so far, but it seems quite useful.

context: My grandmother just got her first smartphone.
pairs.strong: Now every morning at 4 a.m. I get a sparkly owl saying good morning.
pairs.flat: Now she sends me a message every morning, which is nice of her.

context: I asked my doctor how to live longer.
pairs.strong: He said walk ten thousand steps a day. So now I lose my keys on purpose.
pairs.flat: He said I should walk more every day and try to eat more vegetables.

context: My cat knocks one thing off the table every morning.
pairs.strong: She makes eye contact first, like a hostage negotiator.
pairs.flat: She does it every day and then I have to clean it up.

context: I'm thirty-five and I still can't fold a fitted sheet.
pairs.strong: I roll it into a ball and hide it, like evidence.
pairs.flat: I find it hard, so I usually just give up on it.

context: My son asked me why the sky is blue.
pairs.strong: I said, Google it. He said, I did, it said ask your dad.
pairs.flat: I didn't know the answer, so I told him to look it up later.

context: My wife says I never listen to her.
pairs.strong: At least, I think that's what she said.
pairs.flat: She says I don't pay attention to her.

context: I went on a silent retreat for a week.
pairs.strong: Seven days without talking. My wife called it the best holiday she's ever had, and she stayed home.
pairs.flat: We weren't allowed to talk for seven days, which was hard at first, but I got used to it by the end.

context: Indian parents don't say I love you.
pairs.strong: They say: have you eaten? Same thing, plus a threat.
pairs.flat: They show their love in other ways, like cooking.

context: I finally bought a standing desk.
pairs.strong: Now I scroll Instagram at a much more professional height.
pairs.flat: Now I stand up while I work, which is better for my back.

context: My boss told me there's no I in team.
pairs.strong: I said there's no U in raise either, so we're even.
pairs.flat: He wanted me to be more of a team player at work.

context: I tried meditating to calm down.
pairs.strong: Twenty minutes in I'd planned my funeral and an argument I'm having in 2031.
pairs.flat: It was hard to stop thinking about other things, so I stopped after twenty minutes.

context: My uncle says he's found a cure for jet lag.
pairs.strong: He never leaves the house.
pairs.flat: He drinks a lot of water.

context: I told my kids I'd take them somewhere they'd never forget.
pairs.strong: So I took them to the dentist.
pairs.flat: So I took them to the beach.

context: I've been learning to cook from YouTube.
pairs.strong: So far I'm an expert at skipping ads and burning rice.
pairs.flat: So far I've made a few simple dishes, mostly rice and dal.

context: My mother kept the kitchen like a clock.
pairs.strong: Her bangles counted out the rice, a bright brass tick.
pairs.flat: She was very organised whenever she cooked for us.

context: The city never sleeps, they say.
pairs.strong: It lies awake like me, and counts its sirens.
pairs.flat: It is always busy and noisy late at night.

context: I left the village at nineteen.
pairs.strong: The river followed me a mile, then let me go.
pairs.flat: I felt quite sad when I left my home behind.

context: Grief is not a visitor.
pairs.strong: It is a tenant. It pays no rent. It knows where the spoons are.
pairs.flat: It stays with you for a long time after someone dies, and it is hard.

context: My father's hands were rough.
pairs.strong: Sandpaper prayers he never said out loud.
pairs.flat: He worked hard and didn't share feelings.

context: The monsoon came late that year.
pairs.strong: The fields cracked open like mouths that had forgotten the word for water.
pairs.flat: There was a drought and the fields were very dry, and the farmers were worried.

context: We were young and broke and certain.
pairs.strong: We split one chai and called it a feast, and it was.
pairs.flat: We didn't have much money, but we were happy then.

context: She asked me what home means.
pairs.strong: Home is the door that knows my knock.
pairs.flat: Home is where I feel comfortable.

context: The hospital at night is quiet.
pairs.strong: Only the machines keep talking, beep by beep, a borrowed heartbeat.
pairs.flat: There are a lot of machines in the rooms, and they make some noise.

context: I used to be afraid of the dark.
pairs.strong: Now I fear the phone's blue glow at 3 a.m., and the names that never light it.
pairs.flat: Now I am more worried about other things, like my phone and people not calling.

context: Old love letters in a shoebox.
pairs.strong: Paper gone soft as skin, ink gone the colour of tea.
pairs.flat: They are very old now and the writing has faded.

context: My grandmother forgot my name last spring.
pairs.strong: But she still hums the song she sang me, and her hands still know the tune.
pairs.flat: She has memory problems now because of her age, but she remembers some music.

context: The train pulled out at dawn.
pairs.strong: And every window held a different goodbye.
pairs.flat: A lot of people were leaving the city then.

context: They told us to be quiet, to be small.
pairs.strong: So we grew roots instead, and roots are loud underground.
pairs.flat: But we didn't listen to them, and we kept going anyway.

context: Winter in Delhi.
pairs.strong: Fog swallows the streetlights whole and coughs them up as ghosts.
pairs.flat: It gets very foggy and it is hard to see the streetlights.

context: I learned to swim at forty.
pairs.strong: The water held me the way no one had, without asking why.
pairs.flat: It was difficult at my age, but I managed to do it in the end.

context: Every night my neighbour plays the violin.
pairs.strong: Thin notes climb the stairwell like a cat that wants to be let in.
pairs.flat: I can hear the music through the wall of my flat most evenings.

context: After the divorce I kept the plants.
pairs.strong: They didn't know anything had ended; they leaned toward the window anyway.
pairs.flat: I looked after them by myself after that, and they kept growing quite well.

context: My first salary came in an envelope.
pairs.strong: I held it like a diya, cupped against the wind, all the way home.
pairs.flat: I was very proud of it and careful with it on the way back home.

context: Rain on a tin roof.
pairs.strong: A thousand small drums, a clatter, a hush, the sky rehearsing on us.
pairs.flat: It made a lot of noise whenever it rained, especially at night.

context: We've talked about climate change for thirty years.
pairs.strong: Thirty years of talking. Not one more year of waiting. Starting tonight, we act.
pairs.flat: We should probably try to do something more about it in the next few years.

context: My grandfather walked six miles to school.
pairs.strong: He didn't walk six miles so I could stand still.
pairs.flat: He worked hard for his education, and I'm grateful.

context: Some people say this city is too divided to change.
pairs.strong: They said that about every city that ever changed.
pairs.flat: I don't really agree with them about that point.

context: Teachers are underpaid in this country.
pairs.strong: We trust them with our children and pay them like we don't.
pairs.flat: They should get paid quite a bit more than they do now.

context: I'm asking you for one thing tonight.
pairs.strong: Not your money, not your time. Your voice, on Tuesday, at the ballot box.
pairs.flat: Please think about going to vote in the next election if you are able to.

context: When I started this company we had three people and a borrowed laptop.
pairs.strong: We didn't have a plan. We had a promise, and we kept it.
pairs.flat: It was a very small company back then, and it grew slowly.

context: We are told that kindness is weakness.
pairs.strong: Kindness is not weakness. It is strength that has decided not to hurt you.
pairs.flat: I think that being kind to other people is actually a good thing to do.

context: Graduates, the world you're walking into is a mess.
pairs.strong: Good. Messes are where the work is, and the work is where you'll find yourselves.
pairs.flat: It will be hard sometimes, but I think most of you will be okay in the end.

context: Every day, a girl in this district walks past a school she can't attend.
pairs.strong: Not tomorrow. Not next year. Today, we open that door.
pairs.flat: We hope to improve access to education here in the future.

context: My opponent says he'll fix the roads.
pairs.strong: He's had ten years. The only thing he's fixed is the date of his next promise.
pairs.flat: He has been in office for a long time, and the roads are still in bad condition.

context: People ask why I run marathons at sixty.
pairs.strong: Because the finish line doesn't check your birth certificate.
pairs.flat: Because I enjoy running and I want to stay healthy as I age.

context: We lost the final by one goal.
pairs.strong: One goal. One season. One team that will be back, and back hungrier.
pairs.flat: We were disappointed, but we will try again next season with the same team.

context: Science doesn't care about your politics.
pairs.strong: Gravity doesn't vote. Viruses don't read the news.
pairs.flat: Scientific facts are true whatever people think.

context: To the volunteers in this room.
pairs.strong: You didn't wait to be asked. You saw a gap and you became the bridge.
pairs.flat: Thank you very much for all of your help with the project this year.

context: I was told I was too loud, too young, too much.
pairs.strong: So I got louder. And here I am.
pairs.flat: But I didn't let it stop me.

context: Our hospital has one doctor for every five thousand people.
pairs.strong: You wouldn't run a shop like that. Why are we running lives like that?
pairs.flat: We need to hire more doctors at the hospital so that people can be seen sooner.

context: They say one person can't change anything.
pairs.strong: Every change you have ever seen began with one person who refused to agree.
pairs.flat: But I think that individuals can make a difference in some situations, sometimes.

context: As your class president, I've made mistakes.
pairs.strong: I'll own every one of them, and I'll fix every one I can.
pairs.flat: I'm sorry about some of the things that happened this year.

context: Water is life, we say.
pairs.strong: Then why do we treat it like a bill and not a birthright?
pairs.flat: We should all be more careful about how much water we use.

context: Let me end with my mother's words.
pairs.strong: She said: carry your people with you, or don't bother arriving.
pairs.flat: She always told me to think about my family and where I came from.
